dialect.detail: Likely GnuCOBOL (open-source) targeting Linux/Windows with LINE SEQUENTIAL files and CSV data sources; Spanish-language identifiers and prompts suggest Latin American academic context

purpose.domain_detail: Restaurant management system handling menu (carta), dishes (platillos), waiters (meseros), tables (mesas), and orders (pedidos)
purpose.summary: A restaurant management program with a main menu offering 10 options: displaying the menu card, listing dishes by type, registering waiters and tables, recording orders, and various reporting functions. It reads and writes CSV files for persistent storage of restaurant data.

notable_features: Multiple LINE SEQUENTIAL CSV file I/O (5 files)
CONTINUE used as line continuation (non-standard usage)
OPEN OUTPUT overwrites files on each registration (no append)
Incomplete/buggy code: EOF not declared, SET EOF TO TRUE without 88-level, IF Platillos-Tipo = Platillos-Tipo always true
END PROGRAM instead of STOP RUN at end
No COMP-3 or packed decimal usage
verdict.notes: The code has several bugs: EOF is referenced without being declared as an 88-level condition, the condition IF Platillos-Tipo = Platillos-Tipo is a tautology, OPEN OUTPUT is used instead of OPEN EXTEND for appending records, and CONTINUE is misused as a line continuation marker. The program appears to be a student exercise for a restaurant domain, likely written in Spanish-speaking Latin America. The END PROGRAM statement at the end is unusual placement after REGISTER-PEDIDO without a proper paragraph structure.
